title: PRD: Staged Embargo Windows and Staggered Rollout Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the product and operational requirements for staged embargo windows and staggered rollouts. The goal is to provide a repeatable, low-risk process for introducing new serving features, model variants, or pricing-impacting changes while maintaining SLOs and clear commercial signaling to customers.

Scope
- Applies to changes that affect latency, throughput, per-token economics, billing signals, or model fidelity visible to customers.
- Includes: model variant introductions, quantization/precision changes, routing or shard reconfiguration, billing/crediting scheme changes, and new runtime features that alter consumption.
- Excludes: purely client-side SDK UX tweaks, non-customer-facing telemetry reorganizations.

Background and motivation
Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments. Several recent incidents have shown that broad rollouts for changes that slightly alter per-token cost or latency can cause localized customer outages or unexpected bill impacts. A formalized staggered rollout pattern with defined embargo windows lets product, infra and GTM coordinate migrations with minimal customer disruption while providing predictable commercial treatment.

Summary of proposal
We propose a standardized staging and embargo model made up of:
1) Tiered rollout cohorts (dev/smoke, pilot customers, small cohort, large cohort, GA).
2) Per-cohort embargo windows where customers are proactively notified and pricing/credit rules are set.
3) Automated telemetry gates and SLO checks that must pass before promoting to the next cohort.
4) A rollback recipe with fast-fail thresholds and communication templates.
5) Billing reconciliation and crediting rules tied to cohort membership and observed delta.

Requirements (high level)
1. Cohorts and eligibility
   - R1.1: Define 5 rollout cohorts: internal-dev, canary (1–5% traffic), pilot (invite-only), ramp (10–50% traffic), GA (100%).
   - R1.2: Support grouping by customer attribute (tier, region, contract type) and by route/model.

2. Embargo window and communication
   - R2.1: Each cohort must have an embargo window (start/end timestamps) that is recorded in the release metadata.
   - R2.2: A communication template and a channel list (email, product console banner, account manager notice) must be attached to embargo records.
   - R2.3: For contract-impacting changes, allow a 14-day advance notification for enterprise customers and a 7-day notice for self-serve customers where feasible.

3. Telemetry gates and automation
   - R3.1: Define gate checks: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency delta thresholds, token-per-request cost delta, error-rate increase, queue length/backpressure indicators, and regression in model quality metrics (where applicable).
   - R3.2: Gates run continuously for the cohort window. Promotion to the next cohort requires 48 hours of stable metrics within thresholds unless manually overridden with documented rationale.
   - R3.3: Gate configuration must be editable by release owners and stored in versioned release artifacts.

4. Billing and credit handling
   - R4.1: When a new variant introduces a net delta in per-token billed units or credit consumption > 5% for a cohort, a reconciliation plan must be attached.
   - R4.2: Provide an automated crediting tool to issue pro-rated credits to pilot/ramp customers where the change led to measurable adverse cost impact.

5. Rollback and failover
   - R5.1: Define fast-fail thresholds (e.g., >20% p99 latency regression or >3x error increase sustained for 5 minutes) that trigger automatic rollback to the previous variant.
   - R5.2: Support partial rollbacks (by route, region, or tenant) and define the API for targeted rollback operations.

6. Auditability and compliance
   - R6.1: All embargo windows, cohort promotions, gate decisions and manual overrides must be logged with actor, timestamp, and rationale.
   - R6.2: Release artifacts must include a short summary of telemetry analyzed and a final sign-off record.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR1: Rollout orchestration commands must complete within 30s for cohort size changes up to 10% traffic reallocation.
- NFR2: Telemetry and gating systems must operate at 1-minute resolution with retention for 90 days by default.
- NFR3: Operational runbook must guarantee the ability to execute a staged rollback within 5 minutes of threshold breach.

Product and API surface
- Release Manifest (JSON) fields (example):
  - release_id, variant_id, cohorts: [{name, selector, traffic_percentage}], embargo_windows: [{cohort, start, end, notice_sent}], gate_config_id, billing_reconciliation_id, owner, signoffs.
- High-level API endpoints expected:
  - POST /releases (create manifest and schedule cohorts)
  - PATCH /releases/{id}/promote (advance cohort)
  - POST /releases/{id}/rollback (targeted rollback payload: routes/regions/tenants)
  - GET /releases/{id}/telemetry (summarized gate reports)
  - POST /releases/{id}/credits (trigger crediting action for affected customers)

Telemetry and SLOs
- Minimum gate metrics and thresholds (initial defaults):
  - p50 latency delta: < 15%
  - p95 latency delta: < 25%
  - p99 latency delta: < 35%
  - error-rate delta: < 2x baseline or absolute increase < 0.5%
  - token-cost delta: < 5% (billing units) per request
  - model fidelity regression: no statistically significant drop in shadow evals (shadow-eval drift < threshold defined per prompt set)

- SLO linkage: The release gating system must compare cohort metrics to the per-route SLOs maintained in the SLO registry and block promotion if an SLO breach is detected.

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
1. Pre-release (owners: product+release-engineering)
   - Draft release manifest and gate configs.
   - Run simulated traffic using the staging traffic runner for target cohorts.
   - Prepare communication templates and update embargo metadata.

2. Canary (internal-dev -> canary)
   - Execute POST /releases to schedule canary.
   - Monitor gates for a minimum of 24 hours.
   - If gates pass, prepare pilot invites and billing reconciliation plan.

3. Pilot -> Ramp
   - Send pilot customer notices according to the embargo window.
   - Advance cohorts using PATCH /releases/{id}/promote.
   - Collect qualitative feedback from pilot tenants and reconcile cost deltas.

4. Ramp -> GA
   - After 48–72 hours of stable telemetry in ramp, finalize signoffs and lift embargo.
   - Trigger automated crediting if reconciliation plan calls for it.

5. Rollback scenario
   - If a gate fails or a fast-fail threshold triggers, execute targeted rollback: POST /releases/{id}/rollback with affected selectors.
   - Notify stakeholders and open an incident if SLOs are impacted.
   - Postmortem and customer communication template triggered immediately.

Failure modes and mitigation
- Undetected fidelity regression: require a shadow-eval before pilot with an explicit approval step; maintain a pre-run prompt set for key clients.
- Billing surprise: use a preflight estimator to simulate expected per-tenant delta; require finance signoff for changes predicted >10% per-tenant net cost change.
- Automation misfire: provide a manual override path with two-person authorization for rollouts that affect enterprise contracts.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics
- Acceptance: Release artifacts defined, gate configs deployed, communication templates saved, pilot customers signed up, first pilot rollout completed without SLO breaches.
- Success metrics (first 90 days post-GA):
  - Median rollout time from canary to GA: <= 10 days.
  - % of rollouts requiring full rollback: < 5%.
  - Mean customer bill variance attributable to rollout changes (per impacted tenant): < 3% after credits.
  - Time to detect fidelity regression: < 4 hours from deployment.

Ownership and responsibilities
- Product (owner): define manifest, commercial policy, and pilot selection.
- Release Engineering: implement release API, cohort enforcement, and gate automation.
- Observability: provide gate dashboards, alerting, and telemetry retention.
- Finance: preflight cost simulation and crediting authority.
- Customer Success: pilot outreach and post-release communications.

Migration and commercial considerations
- For customers on committed Dedicated contracts, provide an opt-out window and specific schedule in the embargo record.
- Billing reconciliation will default to an automated credit for self-serve customers; enterprise customers may be handled via account manager agreements.

Operational runbooks (quick commands)
- Sample release manifest (JSON snippet):
  {
    \"release_id\": \"rls-2025-06-10-01\",
    \"variant_id\": \"v2-quantized\",
    \"cohorts\": [{\"name\": \"canary\", \"selector\": \"internal\", \"traffic_percentage\": 1}],
    \"embargo_windows\": [{\"cohort\": \"pilot\", \"start\": \"2025-06-20T00:00Z\", \"end\": \"2025-07-04T00:00Z\"}]
  }

- Example CLI to promote cohort: redwoodctl releases promote --id rls-2025-06-10-01 --cohort ramp
- Example CLI to rollback a region: redwoodctl releases rollback --id rls-2025-06-10-01 --selector region:eu-west-1

Open questions and next steps
- Q1: What is the acceptable minimum cohort duration for low-risk rollouts (should we allow 6-hour promotions?) Proposed: keep 48 hours as default but allow 6-hour exception with two-person approval.
- Q2: Should credits be automated or require finance signoff at threshold >10%? Proposed: auto-issue credits for self-serve up to 10%, finance signoff above 10%.
- Next steps: prototype release manifest schema, implement telemetry gate runner for one critical route, run a lab experiment rolling a quantized variant with staged cohorts.

Appendix
- Communication templates (short):
  - Pilot notice: \"We will enable an experimental model variant for your tenant between START and END. Expect no action required; please report any regressions to #pilot-feedback.\"
  - Post-rollback customer note: \"We observed an unexpected regression and have reverted to the previous model variant. We are investigating and will follow up with a timeline. Credits will be applied where applicable.\"

- Links to related docs: release scheduler spec, canary scheduler economics, crediting-tool API (see related_pages).
